gaps.sentence: I put ___ sugar in your tea by mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Too much' is used before uncountable nouns like sugar; 'too sugar' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the three routes avoids the toll entirely.
gaps.hint: not any of three or more
gaps.explanation: 'None of' is used for three or more; 'neither' only for two.

gaps.sentence: She gave the children two sweets ___.
gaps.hint: distribution per child at the end of the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'Two sweets each' means two per child; 'every' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room in here for a piano.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough room' means sufficient space; the negative 'isn't' shows the space is insufficient.

gaps.sentence: Where are the ___ guests? Haven't they arrived yet?
gaps.explanation: 'The other guests' uses 'other' as an adjective; 'others' is a pronoun and cannot precede the noun.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ interruptions this year, so the ceremony ran far more smoothly.
The night bus runs ___ twenty minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Every twenty minutes' expresses regular intervals; 'each twenty minutes' is not used.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.
